condition: acute mesenteric ischemia presenting with abrupt severe diffuse abdominal pain in an older adult taking daily diltiazem for a longstanding irregular heartbeat
level_rationale: Abrupt-onset severe pain across the entire abdomen starting 1 hour ago in a 75-year-old adult taking daily diltiazem for a longstanding irregular heartbeat raises high suspicion for cardioembolic acute mesenteric ischemia requiring immediate emergency hospital computed tomography angiography and vascular or surgical intervention, whereas passing hard dry stools twice over the past 7 days on daily diltiazem reflects subacute calcium-channel-blocker constipation warranting a routine outpatient physician visit.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + diltiazem-associated subacute constipation outpatient control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 75, chronic daily diltiazem for a longstanding irregular heartbeat, and abrupt severe diffuse abdominal pain 1 hour ago) with finite clause coordination ('and receive' / 'and take'), a 1-word span difference (16 vs 17 words), 10 shared trailing tokens, and zero diagnosis labels. Specifying a longstanding rate-controlled irregular heartbeat on daily diltiazem prevents stranding new-onset arrhythmia while anchoring the Rule A control (passing hard dry stools twice over 7 days, a classic diltiazem gastrointestinal side effect shifting level 4 hospital care to level 2 routine doctor care) with zero stated negatives.
